chunks: ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Yaʿfūr narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

If the صاحبُ الْحَقِّ is satisfied with the oath of the one denying his right, and he asks him to swear, and he swears that he has no right against him, then the oath removes the claimant’s right, and he has no claim.

I said: Even if he has just evidence? He said: Yes, even if after making him swear by Allah he were to produce fifty sworn testimonies, he would have no right, for the oath has nullified everything he had previously claimed against him concerning that over which he had made him swear.

key_terms.أَبْطَلَتْ: nullified or invalidated in legal effect
key_terms.الْحَقِّ: the right or due being claimed
key_terms.الْمُنْكِرِ: the defendant who denies the claimed right
key_terms.بِيَمِينِ: by an oath; the formal sworn denial used in adjudication
key_terms.عَادِلَةٌ: just and valid in legal standing
key_terms.قَسَامَةً: multiple sworn testimonies or oaths presented as legal proof

ai.seo_question: Does a defendant’s oath cancel a claimant’s right in Shia hadith, even if the claimant later brings evidence?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning judicial oaths: if a claimant accepts the defendant’s oath and the defendant swears denial, the claimant’s case is nullified. Even later evidence does not revive that claim once the oath has been administered regarding it.
